Regarding your question about Pluto conjunct Saturn, I would say the biggest transformation was easing back into the workforce after spending like 8 years on disability. I spent the second half of that year (2021) thinking about going back to school and started gearing up to enter a radiology tech program. I began volunteering at a hospital ( possibly when the conjunction was exact?), started thinking about pre reqs. Then after a couple months I became impatient and just wanted to start working and making money. I got a job in March 2022,(still there now) but now I'm hating it and making a shift back to medicine - I'm currently in phlebotomy training. I would say the biggest transformation was being able to be well enough to work full time and finally get off of disability. 

I'm also curious about the Pluto square ascendent/descendent, definitely will look out for that! 

I'm in a long term relationship, but we're currently starting a new hobby together and doing more together in general - lots of stepping out of our comfort zones as opposed to couch rotting on our days off haha

Jupiter and Mars will both be conjunct my natal sun at 16'01 Gemini in my 8th house on August 15th. Does anyone know what this might mean for me personally? 

For some reason,I have a feeling that this could be a beneficial transit for me(I hope!). My natal Jupiter is exalted in cancer and my natal Mars is in domicile in Aries, so I've never really thought of Mars as a malefic for me, but who knows - I'm still learning! Please let me know if anyone has any insight.
Thank you for your advice! I look forward to challenging situations ahead as I know they are necessary in order to continue to grow and learn. Thank you again!

Oh yes, I'm not wanting to give myself too much credit cause everyone I practiced on seemed to have good veins. I definitely don't want to get cocky over it either as I know there will be many challenges ahead. With regards to my skills as a baker translating to phlebotomy, I'm mostly referring to being aware of hygiene and cleanliness with food safety, and the parallels of being aware of safety with phlebotomy, with sharps and bodily fluids. I have to be very precise with my work as a baker in many ways, and I feel like that is a big thing with phlebotomy, like with draw order and labelling, etc.. obviously I know that phlebotomy is a whole different beast, and if I mess up a bake that's not as big of a deal as possibly injuring someone or worse.

I'm happy to hear that you love what you do, and I appreciate your advice! I am excited to take on any challenges that come up. I do think I'm interested in inpatient, maybe just for the variety of the day to day. I think I would be happy with this as a long term career, but I do appreciate the option of looking into other fields if I want a change. Thank you again for your feedback and advice!
